status: PUB-9C PASS-03 BATCH 3 — VERIFIED AUTHORITY EXPANSION
policy: Metadata verified against publisher/authoritative bibliographic records. This source supports plurality of biological individuality criteria and physiological/immune individuation; it does not establish a single universal boundary criterion or civilization-scale individuality.

records.citation: Pradeu, Thomas. 2016. ‘Organisms or Biological Individuals? Combining Physiological and Evolutionary Individuality.’ Biology & Philosophy 31 (6): 797–817. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10539-016-9551-1.
records.whatThisSourceSupports: Biological individuality is not exhausted by one criterion; physiological and evolutionary individuality must be distinguished, and immunological/physiological integration can contribute to organismal individuation.
records.whatThisSourceDoesNotSupport: It does not make immune response a universal membership oracle, does not imply that all symbionts belong to one evolutionary individual, and does not establish civilization-scale organismhood.
records.whereMacroscopicLifeGoesBeyondIt: Macroscopic Life operationalizes multiple boundary dimensions and uses perturbation plus model competition to test candidate higher-order boundaries rather than treating any one philosophical criterion as decisive.
